Maya — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Laura (Commercial Lead) and Marissa (Solutions) to confirm commercial levers; I put a draft pricing matrix together (attached) to illustrate the principal paths. High level:

Option A — Subscription-first (Opex):
• Monthly/annual metered charges: platform fee + per-token inference.
• Lower upfront; predictable monthly charge.
• Support included per tier, optional named SME at extra cost.

Option B — Hybrid (CapEx + annual support):
• One-time license for private runtime + annual platform/support fee.
• We can amortize the license over customer-requested term for procurement (we’ll provide a 3-year amortization example).
• For larger commits we offer a license discount (typical range 10–25% depending on commit and payment timing).

Commercial flex we can offer for Clearline:
- 6-month platform-fee waiver or 50% platform-fee for first two quarters for customers who take a 36-month license and commit to minimum throughput.
- Professional services / migration credits: up to one month of equivalent platform fee as credit for migrations over $75k SOW.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24-hour severity 1 response), Premier (SLA-backed, 4-hour severity 1, dedicated success manager), Enterprise (24/7 with named SME and monthly architecture reviews).

I attached the pricing matrix (sergio_pricing_matrix_v3.xlsx) and a draft SOW for your team to review. Laura — any other items I should include before I send a formal offer to Clearline?

Thanks,

Sergio — thanks for the useful draft. A few commercial recommendations based on similar deals:

1) Offer a dual-track payment profile to make procurement comfortable:
   - Present both a one-time license + annual support (CapEx) and a subscription equivalent (Opex) with a three-year total cost comparison in the cover sheet. Procurement typically likes to see the per-year amortization.

2) Platform fee treatment:
   - For on-prem installs where customer supplies infra, treat the platform fee as a configurable line item. Offer an initial 3–6 month deferral or 50% reduction for customers committing to a 36-month license. Avoid full waivers unless there is a large uplift in license revenue.

3) Discount bands and approvals:
   - Up to 15% discount on license list is approvable by you. 15–25% requires Commercial Director (me). >25% needs VP/Revenue approval.

4) Support tiers (suggested catalog):
   - Standard: 9–5 support, 1 business-day severity 1 ack, 3 business-day resolution target; no named SME.
   - Premier: 24/7 severity 1 ack within 4 hours, named technical lead for escalation, two scheduled architecture checks per quarter.
   - Enterprise: 24/7 with on-call rotation, guaranteed 2-hour on-call response for sev1, named SME + quarterly exec reviews.

5) Migration credits / PS discounts:
   - Offer structured credits: 5% credit on license list when customers sign a SOW for >$100k (can stack with early-payment terms).

6) Compliance artifacts:
   - SOC2 report: standard delivery, no charge. Customized runbooks or bespoke audit assistance billed as a support add-on / PS line item.

If you plan to propose a 6-month platform fee concession, include a clause tying it to the 36-month license and minimum throughput. I can approve up to 18% off list for a restructure that includes the platform deferral; anything deeper I'll need to sign off.

LMK if you want me to draft the specific commercial language — happy to redline.

- Laura
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Maya / Clearline procurement — thanks for the patience. Attached are two sanitized commercial options and a short 3-year amortization comparison:

1) Hybrid CapEx (recommended for finance teams that want capitalized software):
   - One-time license: $720,000 (list) — Clearline starter license for private runtime.
   - Annual platform & support fee: $120,000/year (Premier tier).
   - Migration credit: $24,000 applied if SOW > $100k.
   - Commercial concession: 12% license discount if 36-month term and 60-day upfront payment.
   - Platform fee concession: 50% reduction first two quarters, then full fee thereafter (tied to commitment).

2) Subscription (Opex) — lower upfront, slightly higher 3yr total cost:
   - Annual subscription (includes runtime + Premier support): $350,000/year, billed annually; no license line.
   - Migration credit: 10% PS discount on SOWs >$75k.

Support details: Premier includes 4-hour severity 1 ack, named technical lead, monthly architecture review, and a dedicated success manager. Enterprise level is available by request (named SME on retainer). SOC2 report will be provided as standard; any custom audit assistance quoted separately.
